In recent times, the surge in digitized documents, such as invoices, has generated a critical demand for automatic extraction systems capable of handling their complexity. However, creating robust extraction models for these documents remains difficult due to the rich variety in their layouts and visual structures. To address this, we introduce a new, large-scale dataset comprising 10,000 invoices sourced from 12 diverse European countries. Additionally, we propose a multi-instance learning framework tailored for invoice key-value pair extraction. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach surpasses current state-of-the-art methods.

The EuS/InAs interface is a promising candidate for developing a high-quality, lattice-matched, and high-spin-gap electronic structure, essential for spintronics. This study investigates EuS/InAs systems with a focus on lattice matching and electronic properties, specifically examining three distinct configurations: (1) a free-standing EuS monolayer atop a free-standing InAs monolayer, (2) a free-standing InAs monolayer supported by a EuS substrate, and (3) a fully epitaxial structure where InAs grows epitaxially on a EuS substrate. Our calculations reveal that in all scenarios, the InAs valence band maximum (VBM) aligns closely with the top of the EuS valence band. Notably, the epitaxial configuration demonstrates the strongest lattice matching, with the InAs VBM positioned just 0.03 eV below the EuS VBM. Furthermore, the EuS substrate significantly influences the InAs valence band structure in both the substrate-based and epitaxial cases, whereas the InAs substrate has minimal impact on the EuS monolayer. Finally, the band gap in the epitaxial system is found to be approximately 0.15 eV narrower than that of bulk EuS.

This study presents a streamlined demonstration that every subset of Baire space falling within a Borel Wadge class is defined by a $\Sigma^0_\xi$ formula for some ordinal $\xi < \omega_\omega$. Leveraging this compact proof, we also establish that every such subset belongs to a $\Sigma^0_\xi$ class where $\xi < \omega_\omega$ is an arbitrary large countable fixed point of the Borel Wadge hierarchy.

We introduce ClickTrain, a new framework designed to accelerate convolutional neural network (CNN) training by substituting standard full-image supervision with sparse pixel-level annotations. This approach exploits the fact that many tasks, such as object detection and segmentation, only require identifying a small fraction of an image to localize specific objects. By leveraging this "clicks" data, ClickTrain significantly reduces both computational costs and memory requirements. We validate the framework's efficacy across three major vision tasks—object detection, semantic segmentation, and instance segmentation—demonstrating substantial acceleration without compromising accuracy. Notably, when using click-only labels for segmentation tasks, ClickTrain delivers a 2.5x to 3.5x speedup over traditional full-map supervised training while maintaining equivalent performance.

This paper introduces a representation theorem for bounded distributive residuated lattices (BDRls) utilizing their canonical extensions. We first define the operation of canonical extensions specifically applied to bounded distributive lattices and bounded distributive negation-free residuated lattices (NFRRLs), then demonstrate that the standard rules governing these structures remain valid under such extensions. Consequently, the theorem is established by representing a BRLR as the common subalgebra of its canonical form shared with its respective lattice and negation-free components.

Gravitational wave observatories such as LIGO and Virgo have identified signals from three distinct categories of compact binary mergers: binary neutron stars (BNS), binary black holes (BBH), and mixed systems comprising both neutron stars and black holes (BH-NS). While BNS and BH-NS configurations are expected to emit electromagnetic radiation alongside gravitational waves, BBH mergers generally do not. Consequently, BNS and BH-NS events serve as vital probes for astrophysical phenomena, whereas BBH mergers offer a pure window into the dynamics of strong-field gravity. This study examines the statistical properties of these three source classes, specifically their merger rate distributions and redshift dependencies, by analyzing data from the first three observing runs (O1, O2, and O2a). We find that the combined gravitational wave merger rate for BNS and BH-NS systems is $100^{+300}_{-100}$ Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$, while the BBH merger rate is $23^{+14}_{-12}$ Gpc$^{-3}$ yr$^{-1}$. Furthermore, we observe no significant variation in these rates across the redshift range $0 < z < 1$.

The discovery of the Sun as a host to a giant planet has prompted investigations into whether the frequency of these planets depends on the metallicity of their host stars. While prior studies have indicated that higher stellar metallicity correlates with a greater likelihood of hosting giant planets, the underlying physical mechanisms remain unclear. This research utilizes the Gaia Data Release 2 (GDR2) to analyze the metallicity of 1,000 Sun-like stars ($0.8 < M/M_{\odot} < 1.2$) that possess confirmed giant planets ($J < 8.5$). We identified these candidates by cross-referencing the Gaia Catalogue of Discovered Exoplanets with the ESO Exoplanet Catalogue, then derived their metallicities through spectroscopy from the LAMOST survey. Our findings reveal that the median metallicity of the host stars in this sample closely matches the solar value, showing no significant deviation. Furthermore, the distribution of host star metallicities mirrors the general population of Sun-like stars found in LAMOST. Consequently, the evidence suggests that the presence of a giant planet does not necessitate a host star with super-solar metallicity.

In operations management, Constrained Markov Decision Processes (CMDPs) serve as a fundamental framework for addressing decision-making challenges that must adhere to specific operational limits. This paper introduces a novel CMDP variant known as the Time-Dependent CMDP (TD-CMDP), extending the traditional model to incorporate time-varying state and transition probabilities. We address both the finite and infinite horizon scenarios, proposing solution methodologies for each. Specifically, we adapt the successive linearization algorithm to tackle finite horizon problems, while utilizing dynamic programming for its infinite horizon counterpart.

Handwritten form recognition serves as a valuable tool for analyzing student problem-solving strategies in math. While existing systems effectively identify symbols, they struggle to precisely segment them, a difficulty arising from the diverse shapes and structures of these elements. To address this, we introduce a novel approach utilizing a specialized 3D convolutional neural network for segmenting handwritten symbols in equations. This method was evaluated on a new dataset comprising 1,000 images of symbols derived from student work. The results demonstrate that this 3D technique outperforms current state-of-the-art 2D methods.

We investigate superconformal quantum mechanics defined on a resolved conical singularity $\tilde{X}$, where $X$ represents a Calabi-Yau cone. In this framework, BPS states correspond precisely to twisted Dolbeault cohomology classes on the resolved space $\tilde{X}$. Consequently, the BPS spectrum is determined entirely by the resolution geometry, specifically its structure sheaf and associated line bundles. This spectral data is further modulated by a bundle of charges, which encodes information regarding the specific choice of resolution.

This study examines the interplay between an epidemic spreading process and an antiepidemic vaccination process within heterogeneous networks. We develop a mean-field approach to analyze the combined dynamics of these processes, establishing conditions for the stability of the disease-free equilibrium and characterizing the endemic equilibrium. Numerical simulations are conducted to illustrate the theoretical findings, revealing that the heterogeneous structure of the network can increase disease prevalence compared to homogeneous networks, although this structural heterogeneity accelerates the response of the antiepidemic vaccination.

Actor-critic methods are widely recognized for their effectiveness in reinforcement learning, yet they frequently become trapped in local optima. Integrating Hamiltonian Monte Carlo (HMC) offers a solution by enabling more efficient exploration of the policy landscape. This paper introduces a new algorithm, which we term "Hamiltonian Actor-Critic," that unifies these concepts. Our theoretical analysis demonstrates that under specific conditions, the proposed method converges to a global optimum, a claim supported by both numerical simulations and real-world experiments.

For any prime $p \geq 5$, the number can only take the forms $6k \pm 1$ where $k$ is an integer. This principle allows for the elimination of composite numbers of these forms from sequences to identify primes. This work examines the properties of such composite numbers and utilizes them to develop the "Sieve of $6k \pm 1$." This sieving method is then applied to derive closed-form expressions for $\sum_{p \leq x} \frac{1}{p}$ and $\sum_{p \leq x} \frac{1}{\sqrt{p}}$ within the interval $(1, x]$.

This paper introduces a new probabilistic framework for robot localization that leverages a wide range of sensor modalities and effectively manages the specific noise profiles unique to each. Standard data sources, such as camera images, often undergo degradation due to adverse conditions like darkness or rain, causing them to become unreliable; our solution addresses this by dynamically weighting sensor contributions to the localization process to accommodate their individual noise characteristics. The proposed method was rigorously validated through extensive experiments conducted on a physical mobile robot, utilizing a dataset that encompasses diverse environments and scenarios.

The spectral characteristics of small celestial bodies, such as asteroids and cometary nuclei, are typically categorized into three groups: reddish, neutral, or extremely red. While the origins of the first two are reasonably well-understood, the cause of the third remains uncertain. This study investigates the hypothesis that objects displaying a neutral-sloped spectrum might actually consist of a mixture of icy and rocky materials. We conducted numerical simulations of light scattering using a binary aggregate composed of water ice and silicate grains, utilizing the T-matrix method to calculate the individual particle scattering matrices and the discrete dipole approximation to model inter-particle interactions. Our results indicate that a neutral-sloped spectrum emerges when particles of both types are randomly distributed within the aggregate and when their sizes are comparable to one another. Furthermore, we observed that the scattering properties of these mixed aggregates differ significantly from those of single-material aggregates, a phenomenon attributed to the mutual shadowing effects between dissimilar particle types.

Let $T_n(q)$ represent the ring consisting of $n \times n$ lower triangular matrices with entries from the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. This work examines a specific class of affine planes, denoted as $\Pi(T_n(q))$, which are defined over this ring. In this context, every point within the plane $\Pi(T_n(q))$ corresponds uniquely to a non-free cyclic submodule of $T_n(q)$. The study establishes that the incidence structure of points and lines in this plane is isomorphic to the affine plane $\Pi(\mathbb{F}_q^n)$ defined over the full matrix ring $M_n(q)$, with the crucial distinction that $\Pi(T_n(q))$ contains exactly half the number of points.

This work examines the $\mathcal{P}$-generic extensions of the form $V^{\mathcal{P}}$, where $\mathcal{P}$ represents the forcing notion for reals that are simultaneously Cohen and random over a base model. The study focuses on the relationships between the continuum's cardinal characteristics and the coexistence of both types of reals within $V^{\mathcal{P}}$. In particular, we establish the existence of a model containing $\mathcal{P}$-generic extensions devoid of random reals, and another in which every real possesses the structure of a mix of Cohen and random components.

Recent Bayesian approaches to dynamic treatment regimes have incorporated the pessimism principle to enhance safety by prioritizing models that minimize potential regret under uncertainty. This study introduces a new Bayesian learner that applies the pessimism principle specifically to the outcome regression function. By employing a conditional variance pessimism metric, we aim to decrease the estimated value of actions exhibiting high variance, thereby encouraging more consistent decision-making. Using a Gaussian process for the outcome regression function allows for straightforward derivation of the resulting posterior distribution. This posterior distribution enables the construction of a posterior-based counterfactual ensemble, which facilitates the efficient sampling of counterfactual data necessary for performing importance sampling. Empirical evaluations on both synthetic data and a real-world clinical dataset demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms standard Bayesian learners by achieving superior balance between effectiveness and safety.

This paper introduces a new family of tilting modules derived from simple bimodules, specifically $I \otimes_{\lambda} -$, where $\lambda$ represents a two-sided ideal and $I$ denotes a simple bimodule within the category of finitely generated $\lambda$-$\lambda$-bimodules. We demonstrate that these constructed tilting modules maintain the property of being both projective and injective. The work further provides explicit examples of such modules within the realm of Artin algebras, proving their relevance as projective or injective tilting objects. Additionally, the text generalizes and extends an existing dual form of tilting theory proposed by Miyashita.

The paper demonstrates the root system of $E_8$ by utilizing the Macbeath icosahedral 3-design and the binary 16-gon. The method constructs the Macbeath design from the $A_7$ root system and subsequently derives the $E_8$ root system through the use of the $E_7$ extended structure.

This study investigates the low-energy excitations of a flat-band superconductor, defined by a Hamiltonian featuring a perfectly flat band and an isolated, completely filled band situated at lower energies. In this configuration, the flat band's superconducting order parameter is determined by the composite order parameter of the lower band. Our findings indicate that while the system supports dispersive bosonic excitations, the electrons within the flat band remain strictly immobile. Furthermore, we identify a set of topological surface states residing on the system's boundaries.

The generalized Polya theorem establishes that the Gaussian distribution is uniquely defined by the complete monotonicity of its squared characteristic function. In contrast, our version of Polya's theorem operates in reverse: it considers the convex function $1-\varphi(t)$, where $\varphi(t)$ represents the characteristic function of a random variable $X$ supported on $[0,1]$. Specifically, if this function is $2\pi$-periodic and convex on the interval $[-\pi, \pi]$, then $\varphi(t)$ must take the form of either a Gaussian or a mixture of Gaussians.

Presence-absence data, which indicate whether a species occupies a specific site, are fundamental in ecology. While methods for analyzing such data are well-established, the case involving spatially correlated absent data (indicating true non-occupancy) remains poorly understood. This study introduces a Bayesian framework for modeling the joint spatial distribution of species presence and absence. By utilizing a copula function, the proposed method links the probability of a species' presence with its absence across spatial locations. The approach is evaluated through both simulated datasets and a real-world dataset concerning the spatial distribution of trees in a forest.

Saliency detection is a critical visual task that identifies significant areas within an image, yet existing methods often struggle with imprecise boundary delineation and inadequate handling of complex contexts. To address these limitations, we propose a new framework called CSDNet, which integrates a cross-attention context extraction module, a multi-scale salient object detection network. The cross-attention mechanism efficiently captures long-range dependencies to generate comprehensive image context, while the multi-scale detection module ensures precise object segmentation. Empirical results demonstrate that this architecture outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches on the COCO-100K and COCO-2014 benchmark datasets.

This study outlines our participation in the SemEval 2019 Task 6, which evaluates systems for identifying abusive tweets. We employed a pre-trained BERT model, fine-tuned it to classify abusive and non-abusive tweets, and leveraged provided train and non-train test datasets. Our method achieved a F1 score of 0.868 on the non-train test set and 0.880 on the train test set, placing us in the top 10% of 1,000+ submissions.

Computed tomography (CT) is a prevalent medical imaging technique that reconstructs a 3D distribution of linear attenuation coefficients from numerous 2D X-ray projections. While most standard CT scanners utilize monochromatic X-rays, polyenergetic sources are frequently employed in specialized applications. However, using a broad spectrum of energies introduces potential artifacts during image acquisition and reconstruction. This study examines a forward model for X-ray data derived from polychromatic sources and a general exponential attenuation law, analyzing it through the lens of Fredholm integral equations of the second kind. We demonstrate that, under certain conditions, this forward model can be approximated by a discretized form of the Abel integral equation. By applying established solution methods for the Abel equation to this discretized approximation, we derive an explicit formula for inverting the forward model. Finally, we validate our analytical findings with simulations of synthetic CT data.

This paper introduces a new dataset comprising handwritten historical letters from the 18th and 19th centuries, featuring transcriptions and annotations for handwriting classification. These documents, created by Scottish emigrants who settled in Australia and New Zealand, were transcribed and imaged by volunteers. We address the challenge of recognizing handwriting in handwriting-inclusive low-resource environments, a task particularly difficult due to the scarcity of training data and variations in writing styles across time and geography. To overcome these hurdles, we developed a H2H2TC (Handwritten Historical Text Classification) model, which leverages the interdependence between characters within a word. Experiments conducted on the HTR22 benchmark demonstrate that our model surpasses existing state-of-the-art methods.

This study examines atomic nuclei with $N=28$ and $N=50$ neutron counts, focusing on the impact of the $E_{3\text{max}}$ truncation within the truncated configuration interaction (TCI) framework. Our findings indicate that calculations employing $E_{3\text{max}}$ converge rapidly toward exact results for these systems. Furthermore, this convergence rate is governed by the magnitude of the three-body interaction strength; consequently, the inclusion of such forces significantly enhances nuclear predictions when paired with a truncated basis.

The Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model serves as a quintessential example of a one-dimensional topological phase, characterized by a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ topological invariant. In this study, we investigate the SSH model within a finite system subject to open boundary conditions, utilizing the density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) method to examine its ground-state properties. Our findings reveal that the energy spectrum aligns perfectly with analytical predictions, while the bond- and site-resolved occupation numbers exhibit distinct peaks at the system boundaries, indicative of zero-energy edge modes. Furthermore, we analyze the convergence of the site and bond bases and determine the optimal truncation point for the bond basis required to accurately capture the characteristics of these topological edge states.

This study investigates the compactness properties of composition operators defined on the Bergman spaces of specific bounded convex domains within $\mathbb{C}^n$, particularly those featuring non-trivial analytic discs on the boundary. We further provide necessary and sufficient conditions for when a composition operator associated with an arbitrary symbol is compact acting on the Bergman space of the polydisc.

In this model, a primary method generates numerous instances that operate independently in parallel. This study introduces a novel, optimized implementation of the Cooley-Tukey FFT designed for the Apple M1 architecture, which leverages Unified Shimmer Architectures (UMA). Built upon the Apple M1's Unified Shimmer Architectures (UMA), this study presents a new, optimized implementation of the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) designed specifically for Apple M1 chips. This implementation utilizes the Single-Method Multiple-Objects (SMMO) approach, where a central algorithm spawns multiple independent instances that execute in parallel. We propose universal family $U(1)_X$ models featuring a new abelian gauge symmetry that violates R-parity, thereby allowing the lightest odd particle to serve as dark matter. In these frameworks, the model's lightest dark matter candidate is a neutral fermion, specifically a neutralino, which is generated through the super-Higgs mechanism alongside the mass generation for the $U(1)_X$ gauge boson. We examine the implications of this framework for the nature of the dark matter candidate and its phenomenology, specifically analyzing the constraints imposed by $X$-baryon number conservation on the relic density of the dark matter candidate.

Charged particle detector prototypes built for the CERN NA62 experiment utilize 10 mm diameter, 1.5 m long, and 0.25 mm wall-thickness borosilicate glass straw tubes. These dimensions were selected to ensure that the straws could be fabricated with standard industrial techniques and installed within the NA62 detector assembly. To evaluate the mechanical stability of these tubes under high internal pressure, the study measured the Poisson's ratio of 0.25 mm thick straws made from three distinct types of borosilicate glass. The results indicate that a wall thickness of 0.25 mm is sufficient for maintaining structural integrity at the operating pressure of 1.5 bar.

This study examines the issue of maximizing the worst-case probability for any attribute value associated with a decision function, denoted as the $\text{MARmax}$ problem. It is demonstrated that this problem can be reformulated as a linear program, allowing for the derivation of both upper and lower bounds through a specialized bounding approach. Additionally, the research investigates the $\text{MARmin}$ problem, which involves minimizing the maximum posterior probability, and explores the relationship between the bounds of $\text{MARmax}$ and $\text{MARmin}$. Empirical evaluations using the ELI dataset illustrate the practical application of these proposed methods.

We examine an atomic impurity undergoing acceleration within a spin-orbit coupled Bose-Einstein condensate during its supersolid stripe phase. Our findings reveal that while impurities exhibit standard friction within a low-density region, they experience anomalous damping in the supersolid stripe phase. This anomalous effect stems from the exchange of momentum with spin-density waves, leading to a non-monotonic dependence of the damping coefficient on the impurity's velocity.

Within a generalized quadrangle $(\mathcal{P},\mathcal{B},\mathcal{F})$, a subset of points $C \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ forms a $\mathcal{GQ}$-code if every line intersects it in either 0 or 4 lines. This condition is equivalent to stating that $C$ constitutes a $(\mathcal{P},4)$-arc and possesses a minimum distance of 4. This paper establishes that for any $(\mathcal{P},4)$-arc with distance 4, a specific construction yields a code $D$ such that the Hamming distance between any distinct pair of points in $C \setminus D$ and any point in $C \setminus D$ is exactly 8. Consequently, the resulting code $C \cup D$ achieves a minimum distance of 8.

The Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) represents a massive, dense region within the galactic plane of the Milky Way, extending approximately 1,000 parsecs from the galactic center. This study utilizes a novel, high-precision dataset of 12CO(2-1) emission lines to investigate the gaseous density architecture within the CMZ. By applying a new radial density profile model, we determine that the gaseous distribution is highly clumpy, with a mean density of roughly $10^3$ M$_{\odot}$ pc$^{-2}$. This clumpy nature is further supported by the power-law characteristics of the power spectral density of the surface density. Additionally, we examine the relationship between gas and stellar distributions, finding that the gas profile is steeper than the stellar one. These findings indicate that the gas is more centrally concentrated than previously thought, suggesting that earlier models based on smoother density assumptions may have underestimated the central gas-to-stellar mass ratio.

Non-linear effects in X-ray spectroscopy can obscure the electronic and structural information that Non-Dispersive X-ray Absorption Near Edge Spectroscopy (XANES) is meant to reveal. This study examines how fluence alters the non-dispersive XANES spectra of a Cu foil, revealing fluence-specific shifts that expose fluence-induced modifications in both sample structure and electron configuration. To clarify these phenomena, we performed time-resolved XANES and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) on copper exposed to intense X-ray pulses at the European X-ray Free-Electron Laser (Eu-XFEL). The results indicate that during the first few hundred picoseconds post-irradiation, the XANES spectra are modified by the simultaneous occurrence of electron configuration changes and structural rearrangements. Conversely, structural alterations dominate the XANES signal on a millisecond timescale, driving the observed fluence dependence. These findings offer a framework for interpreting and mitigating non-linear artifacts in XANES data, thereby enabling the utilization of the Eu-XFEL for probing ultrafast structural dynamics.

On-chip temperature monitoring is essential for managing thermal loads and ensuring system reliability, particularly in high-performance computing environments. This paper introduces a novel CMOS sensor designed specifically to support dynamic thermal management (DTM) and dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS). The system leverages a low-power, high-precision circuit that converts temperature readings into corresponding adjustments for voltage and frequency. By enabling precise, real-time synchronization of these parameters, the sensor facilitates more aggressive scaling strategies, which in turn allows for higher operating frequencies and voltages before thermal limits are reached.

Quantum correlation polarization entanglement is fundamental to quantum information science and technology. While quantum dots are currently the leading source for generating high-quality entangled photon pairs via spin excitations, achieving precise control over their orientation remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a method for producing polarization entangled photons using the self-interaction of excitons within a single semiconductor microcavity. The proposed architecture is compatible with existing quantum optical platforms and offers a pathway to create other forms of quantum entanglement.

This study investigates the online construction of spanner networks within metric spaces, specifically focusing on the Euclidean line. We establish a competitive ratio lower bound of $\Omega(\sqrt[3]{n})$ for any online $(1 + \frac{1}{n})$-spanner algorithm operating in one dimension. Furthermore, we present an algorithm that matches this bound with a competitiveness of $O(\sqrt[3]{n})$ for the same problem. In contrast to the optimal $O(\log^* n)$ ratio achieved in offline settings, our results indicate that online approaches incur a significantly greater penalty.

Classifying IoT devices is essential for numerous applications, yet it is often hindered by the high costs associated with extracting features from device traffic. To address this limitation, we introduce a new Bayesian framework that jointly models the device classification process and the uncertainty surrounding feature extraction costs. This approach enables the dynamic, real-time allocation of extraction resources, optimizing the balance between classification performance and computational efficiency. We validate the method using a realistic dataset comprising traffic from 1,000 IoT devices representing 100 distinct device types.

G\"odel modal logics arise as natural extensions of intuitionistic modal logic by incorporating the G\"odel-Dummett linearity principle, which asserts that all finite frames possess transitive and dense upward chains. This text introduces the concept of G\"odel-\v{C}omprehension algebras, which serve as the modal counterpart to G\"odel-comprehension structures, and demonstrates that the canonical algebra constructed from any such algebra functions as its own canonical G\"odel-modal algebra. Furthermore, the study establishes an equivalence between varieties of G\"odel-comprehension structures and the classes of G\"odel-modal logics, and examines the relationship between the corresponding frame structures and algebras.

This study introduces a new word alignment approach that leverages external bilingual information from parallel corpora to enhance performance. The methodology employs a probabilistic graphical model to jointly optimize the word alignment task and the estimation of word translation probabilities between two languages. By utilizing the Gold Bilingual Information (GBI) to refine these translation likelihoods, the model achieves more accurate word-to-word mappings. Empirical evaluations conducted on the BLEURT benchmark demonstrate that this method surpasses current state-of-the-art approaches.

This study introduces an asynchronous block-iterative decomposition algorithm designed to tackle Nash equilibrium challenges in generalized convex-concave settings involving interlinked functions. The proposed approach extends prior work by Han et al. (2020), which focused on convex-concave functions, to accommodate scenarios where functions may lack monotonicity. The analysis demonstrates that this generalized method maintains its key advantages, specifically ensuring both convergence to a valid equilibrium and low communication overhead.

Primordial Black Holes (PBHs) are hypothesized to represent PBHs as a potential dark matter candidate. This study investigates PBH formation within the context of a universe containing both dark energy and radiation. We derive exact solutions for the Hubble parameter and scale factor applicable to this model, subsequently utilizing them to calculate the relationship between PBH mass and the expansion scale. Additionally, we examine how the dark energy influence affects the evolution of the horizon of size, alongside an analysis of the resulting PBH mass spectrum.

We present a theoretical framework for describing the phase behavior of monodisperse molecules featuring a rigid core and anisotropic, flexible tails. This model is implemented using a Monte Carlo approach on a lattice, where the shape of each molecule is defined by a wedge. When the rigid core occupies less than half the system's packing density ($\phi < 0.5$), the system undergoes a sequence of phase transitions from an isotropic liquid to a nematic, then a smectic, and finally a cholesteric liquid crystal. Conversely, for packing densities exceeding 0.5 ($\phi > 0.5$), the cholesteric phase transforms into a hexagonal crystal. Notably, the cholesteric ordering in wedge-shaped molecules arises from a distinct mechanism compared to that seen in standard liquid crystals composed of polar molecules.

The study establishes a sufficient condition ensuring the positive definiteness of a specific type of function defined on the sphere, conditioned upon its expansion using Gegenbauer polynomials. Additionally, it provides an expansion criterion for continuous functions that are invariant under the special orthogonal group $SO(n+1, \mathbb{R})$ when integrated against any probability measure.

Standard imaging generally relies on three core components: a light source, an object to be visualized, and a detector. In certain specialized fields, such as astronomy, the ability to control the light source is often impossible, whereas in others, like microscopy, the object itself may be difficult to access or manipulate. This paper proposes an innovative illumination strategy for scenarios where neither the light source nor the target's position is known. The method involves three steps: first, capturing images from multiple vantage points; second, utilizing these images to calculate the locations of all light sources and the objects; and third, applying the derived positional data to synthesize what would appear if the sources and objects were perfectly localized.

Rheological studies of complex liquids flowing across rough surfaces are essential for understanding friction in applications ranging from biological systems to industrial manufacturing. This study investigates the relationship between shear rate and interfacial slip in a model system consisting of a concentrated colloidal silica suspension moving over a surface with microscale square pillars. Experiments reveal three distinct slip regimes: a low-shear-rate regime governed by contact friction, an intermediate regime where slip scales with the square root of the shear rate, and a high-shear-rate regime characterized by slip proportional to the square root of the shear rate. The transition points between these regimes depend on the specific roughness geometry. The observed scaling in the high-shear regime aligns with predictions from rate-state friction theories, suggesting that inertial effects within the bulk fluid drive slip in this limit.

In ISIC challenge 2019, the objective was to diagnose skin malignancies by analyzing images of human lesions. Our approach involved a ResNet-50 convolutional neural network trained on a dataset of 10,000 images representing 8 distinct classes. To address class imbalance, we employed weighted loss functions and oversampled minority classes during validation and testing phases. Additionally, we integrated a data augmentation strategy to artificially expand our training data. Our final submission achieved a weighted F1-score of 0.7203, ranking it as the top performance among all 141 participating teams.

This study examines the electronic structure of the cubic intermetallic compound Cu3Au using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES). The observed spectral features are interpreted using a model that incorporates both the nearly-free-electron approximation and a specific k-dependent potential with cubic symmetry. The research demonstrates that because lifetime broadening is significant, the need for sophisticated theoretical frameworks is reduced. Instead, the empirical model proves highly effective at capturing the essential aspects of the observed ARPES data.

This study examines the free expansion of a gas within an isolated container, a scenario that can be modeled as a thermodynamic process involving a finite timeframe. By applying a Carathéodory-style approach to the equilibrium states of the gas, we demonstrate that the microwork term carries a negative sign. Furthermore, we derive an inequality regarding the magnitude of this signed microwork, which remains valid for any process occurring over a given duration.

We demonstrate that for any symplectic manifold with at least two distinct almost complex structures, the coefficients of the corresponding curvature graphs can be formulated using Stieffl sums and the weights of the associated Hitchin families. This result holds even when those coefficients arise from specific path-ordered integrals involving the curvature and its derivatives.

This study investigates the singularly perturbed Hertzian chain, a model characterized by non-smooth nonlinearity, to demonstrate that non-smooth localized solutions, known as nanoptera, arise through a non-analytic dependence on the $\varepsilon$ parameter. While an asymptotic expansion up to order $O(\varepsilon)$ captures the solution profile, it fails to fully describe the solution's behavior at the origin due to the presence of a Dirac delta function. This limitation highlights a fundamental distinction between smooth and non-smooth localized solutions.

We examine the classical oscillations of a scalar field within an inflationary cosmological framework. Our analysis demonstrates that the mean energy density of this classical oscillating field accurately replicates the behavior of a corresponding quantum expectation value. We further establish the validity of this equivalence across various scenarios, including scenarios involving coupling to other fields or expansion rate variations. Finally, we confirm that this consistency holds regardless of whether the initial conditions for the classical field were derived from quantum theory or established independently.

Let $G$ be a graph and $H$ be a connected graph with a maximum degree of at most 3. We say that $G$ possesses the $H$-pairing property (or $G$ satisfies the PH-property for $H$) if there exists a partition of $G$'s edge set into two subsets, $E_1$ and $E_2$, such that the subgraph formed by $E_1$ is a collection of edge-disjoint copies of $H$, and the subgraph formed by $E_2$ is a path. In this study, we establish the existence of a specific graph $G$ that fails to exhibit the pairing property for any graph $H$ which is not path-like.

We examine the diffusion of a quantum walk involving two degrees of freedom, specifically a three-state model, where the mixing angle $\theta_c$ is not uniform but varies as a function of the lattice site. This study focuses on how this spatially dependent $\theta_c$ influences the diffusion of an initially localized wavepacket. Our analysis reveals that the average walk exhibits characteristics of both diffusion and localization, contingent upon the specific profile chosen for $\theta_c$.

Self-supervised Vision Transformers (ViTs) have recently emerged as a powerful alternative to standard supervised counterparts and convolutional networks (CNNs), particularly for global representation learning. This study investigates their potential for downstream semantic segmentation tasks. We introduce an efficient, global self-supervised strategy specifically adapted for image patches, which leverages the inherent patchification of the ViT architecture. Our experiments across three distinct datasets reveal that these self-supervised ViTs substantially outperform both traditional supervised ViTs and CNNs in terms of representational quality for segmentation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that freezing the model weights acquired through our self-supervised training process yields superior results compared to fine-tuning. Finally, our analysis of the proposed method's loss function offers valuable insights into the specific nature of the learned features.

This study introduces a comprehensive dissipative dark fluid model unifying dissipative dark matter and dark energy. The framework posits that the dark sector comprises a cold dark matter component subject to dissipation and a component of dark energy. The analysis reveals that, within this model, dissipative effects manifest as a time-varying equation of state for dark matter alongside an effective equation of state for the dark energy sector. The study further explores the implications of these variations on the expansion history of the universe and the nature of dark energy.

This study examines the one-dimensional heat equation's Cauchy problem, which is noted as ill-posed due to the fact that not every square-integrable function on the real line serves as a valid initial condition. We introduce a regularization approach by restricting the initial data to a specific subset of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ where the Fourier transform vanishes outside a bounded interval. This constraint enables us to derive upper bounds on the norm of the corresponding solution operator. Additionally, we investigate the sensitivity of these operators to perturbations in the initial data and demonstrate that, even with this regularization, they remain discontinuous.

Image editing and generation are two distinct yet complementary tasks that have gained significant attention in recent years. While image editing involves modifying existing visuals, image generation focuses on creating new content from scratch. We introduce a unified framework that integrates both processes by incorporating semantic guidance (SEGA). This approach allows for the synthesis of new attributes into an input image, effectively bridging editing and generation. We evaluate our method against state-of-the-art alternatives, demonstrating its superior performance.

Recent advancements in predictive analytics have been driven by deep Bayesian learning, which addresses the need for quantifying uncertainty in machine learning models. By separating predictive uncertainty into aleatoric (data-driven) and epistemic (model-related) components, this approach enables more robust decision-making. However, existing methods for analyzing epistemic uncertainty often struggle with aleatoric uncertainty. This study introduces a novel framework for modeling aleatoric uncertainty within convolutional neural networks using a variational approach. By leveraging the shared structure of Bayesian posterior distributions, our method maps the convolutional layers of standard CNNs to the latent space of a specific probabilistic model, specifically a Gaussian Process with a shared kernel. This technique allows for the independent characterization of uncertainty arising from both data and model limitations. Empirical evaluations across three image classification benchmarks demonstrate that this framework effectively captures distinct uncertainty types and delivers state-of-the-art performance.

This study examines the implications of $J/\psi$ decays into invisible states, focusing on light sterile neutrinos with masses below 1 GeV. We demonstrate that existing experimental data from $B$-factories regarding the disappearance of $B$-mesons into these sterile states impose stringent limits on the mixing between light sterile neutrinos and active ones. Consequently, direct searches for light sterile neutrinos within $B$-factories offer a highly sensitive avenue for probing this mixing. Furthermore, we investigate scenarios where the invisible products consist of dark matter particles or axions, which could also be accessible through $B$-factory experiments.

We analyzed high-resolution, full-disk solar images from the Daniel K. Inouye Solar Telescope (DKIST) to investigate magnetic bright points (MBPs) in the photosphere. By applying a novel segmentation technique, we measured the areas and diameters of photospheric magnetic fields. The resulting distributions for both area and diameter follow power laws, with the latter showing a cutoff at approximately 1.5 arcseconds. Additionally, we calculated the mean sizes of these features across various wavelengths and spectral bands.

Humans and machines utilize various visual signals to identify objects and activities, with spatial and temporal context being particularly vital. While current deep learning models for action recognition predominantly rely on pre-trained spatial backbones and treat temporal data as secondary, we introduce a novel approach that treats time as equivalent in importance to space. Our method, named TimeSformer, leverages the self-attention mechanism across both spatial and temporal dimensions to efficiently capture long-range dependencies within video data. This architecture is applied to the challenging task of video action recognition, where it is evaluated against leading models. The results demonstrate that TimeSformer not only establishes a new state-of-the-art performance on the Kinetics-400 dataset but also achieves state-of-the-art results on the NTU RGB-D 60 dataset.

We investigate the cosmological production of dark magnetic monopoles, a scenario that could resolve the absence of monopoles in laboratory settings. In this framework, monopoles form an elliptical distribution due to the gravitational influence of the Milky Way; however, their total mass must remain below current limits imposed by halo ellipticity to be viable. We demonstrate that satisfying this constraint necessitates a monopole mass exceeding 10 TeV, which in turn implies that they can be detected at the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC).

Accurately predicting future weather conditions is vital for addressing climate-related challenges, yet this task is complicated by the scarcity of extensive, high-quality labeled datasets. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a data augmentation strategy that generates synthetic cloud imagery for forecasting purposes. This approach employs a Video Swin-Transformer as a data-driven generative model to create realistic variations of static images by integrating temporal depth information. Evaluated on the Euro4K dataset, our method achieves state-of-the-art results, demonstrating an 18% improvement in Inter-Polish (IP) metrics and an 11% gain in Inter-Polish (IP) scores compared to prior methods.

We examine an extended scalar electroweak framework featuring a complex singlet, which allows for the spontaneous breaking of $Z_2$ symmetry to serve as a dark matter candidate. This model is analyzed within the context of $Z$-boson line shape measurements at LEP, $Z$-pole observables from LEP and SLC, and Higgs production and decay rates constrained by LHC data. We determine the parameter space compatible with experimental results and investigate the phenomenology of the singlet's real component, the proposed dark matter particle.

The PPT square conjecture has been proven for finite dimensions, demonstrating that any positive partial transpose (PPT) state $\rho$ on $H_A\otimes H_B$ can be expressed as $\rho = \sigma^{\Gamma_A}\otimes \tau^{\Gamma_A}$ where the partial transpose is taken with respect to Alice's subsystem. This decomposition involves two PPT states, $\sigma$ and $\tau$, defined on the combined system $H_A\otimes H_B$. 

The PPT square conjecture has been proven for the case of two qubits and one qubit with another of any dimension. This study extends the analysis to show that the inequality holds for the entire space of dimensions $m\times n$. 

The proof relies on demonstrating that the set of all PPT states forms a convex structure. By utilizing this property, the authors establish the result through a sequence of logical steps involving the decomposition of the original PPT state into two other such states. 

The paper concludes by suggesting that the PPT square inequality may serve as a useful tool in quantum information theory, particularly in the study of entanglement theory.

Intracellular transport mechanisms are vital for the development, operation, and endurance of neurons. Defects in these transport systems are frequently linked to neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and Huntington's diseases. To investigate these cellular transport processes, researchers utilize Total Internal Reflection Fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy, a technique that enables the visualization of organelles and proteins within the cell's immediate interior. This study introduces a comprehensive image analysis framework for TIRF microscopy, capable of simultaneously tracking multiple fluorescently labeled structures. By integrating various image processing algorithms, we can determine the precise coordinates of individual objects, calculate their velocities, and generate displacement trajectories. Furthermore, the system automatically identifies and corrects experimental artifacts, such as those resulting from camera noise or drift. Ultimately, this methodology offers a robust means to examine intracellular transport dynamics and holds significant promise for advancing research in cellular biology.

This paper introduces a novel approach for identifying banking fraud by analyzing network motifs within transaction graphs. We evaluate our method using the widely recognized Enron email dataset, comparing its performance against traditional machine learning techniques.

We examine the tidal disruption of a white dwarf star by a black hole, focusing on scenarios where the resulting debris forms a radiation-dominated accretion disk. The process generates both electromagnetic radiation and gravitational waves, with the latter's spectrum and luminosity determined by the white dwarf's mass and radius, as well as the black hole's mass and spin. The analysis covers the full evolution of the system, from the initial tidal disruption through the formation of the disk, to the final merger. The derived gravitational waveforms are applicable to detecting such events using future detectors like LISA.

This article provides an overview of form factors, which are essential for describing the hadronic component of weak and electroweak decay processes. The ratio models developed by Tversky and later extended by Lichtenstein and Keeney are examined in this study. It is demonstrated that the symmetric versions of these models, specifically those defined by Lichtenstein and Keeney, function as metrics only under the condition of weak order completeness. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that both Lichtenstein's and Keeney's formulations, when viewed as metrics, are topologically equivalent to the standard Euclidean metric.

Current motion deblurring techniques relying on synthetic blur data often fail to generate realistic pairs, a limitation that hinders the performance of subsequent deep learning models. Conversely, approaches utilizing real blur data typically struggle with the high cost and scarcity of annotated datasets. To address these issues, we introduce a new framework for creating high-quality blur pairs through a self-supervised cycle consistency method. This method cycles a sharp image through degradation and restoration processes to align the blurred output with the input, effectively recovering the original latent clean image. By employing a pre-trained deblurring network to handle the forward pass, we can reconstruct clear images from unknown or captured degraded inputs without needing actual samples. Experiments confirm that this strategy successfully produces realistic blur pairs and significantly enhances the efficacy of motion deblurring algorithms.

Hebbian learning is a form of unsupervised learning in neural systems that occurs through the correlation of simultaneous pre- and post-synaptic activity, enabling adaptation without external guidance. This review examines the theoretical underpinnings of Hebbian learning alongside its biological and physical implementations. It further explores the diverse computational capabilities of such networks, including tasks like pattern recognition, memory, and optimization.

Consider an ordered set $P$ and an ultrafilter $D$ on the natural numbers. It is a well-known result that the structure $S$ of all sequences in $P$ modulo $D$ forms a linearly ordered set. This paper demonstrates that the upper convex completion of $S$, denoted as $T$, constitutes a completed structure. Specifically, $T$ is shown to be an ultrapower of the natural numbers with respect to $D$. Consequently, $T$ is a complete, densely ordered set without endpoints. This finding provides a method for characterizing all linearly ordered sets that are order-isomorphic to ultrapowers of $P$ with respect to $D$ as precisely those where $S$ is a dense subset.

Benchmark datasets are essential for developing and comparing machine learning algorithms. However, their unique attributes may cause rankings of computational methods to differ significantly from those observed in real-world applications. To address this, we introduce **Benchmark**, a comprehensive, publicly available repository containing 200,000 labeled instances drawn from 14 diverse scientific domains. This dataset enables the creation of bespoke benchmarks tailored to specific research problems. Our analysis reveals that while certain techniques excel on standard benchmarks, their relative performance varies across various domain-specific subsets of our collection.

Hadwiger's coloring conjecture posits that for any graph with chromatic number $k$, a complete graph of order $k$ exists as a Hadwiger minor. In this study, we examine a variation of this problem within the context of distance-$2$ subgraphs. Specifically, we investigate how many colors are needed to color the distance-$2$ subgraph of a graph $G$ such that the resulting chromatic number matches a target $k$, assuming $G$ does not contain a complete subgraph of order $l$ (where $l > k$). We demonstrate that if conjecture holds for the general case, it suffices to verify it only for graphs minor-free with respect to any complete graph $K_{l}$ when targeting chromatic number $k$.

This paper introduces a robust adaptive algorithm for graph signal recovery that is robust to graph mismatches. The approach utilizes a kernel-based cost function with an associated kernel regression least squares solution, where the key innovation is an adaptive mechanism for adjusting signal support. Specifically, the algorithm dynamically refines the kernel width to induce sparsity in the dual domain, thereby enabling resistance to mismatches in the graph structure. Empirical results from both simulated datasets and real-world applications demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy.

We introduce a method for generating and controlling atomically entangled states that are resilient against technical noise, thereby enhancing the performance of noisy-matter-wave interferometry. This approach involves engineering atomic spin-squeezed states using a specific configuration of Ramsey interferometry, which allows for the decoupling of the squeezing property from the final phase accumulation. We demonstrate the viability of these states in a dual-rail atom interferometer, confirming their utility even under conditions of Rayleigh scattering. Furthermore, we illustrate that employing these robust entangled states in a dual-rail setup can achieve phase sensitivity surpassing the standard quantum limit, specifically in the context of dark-matter detection.

This study examines the anisotropic $p$-Laplace operator within a domain $D$ defined by the equation $\frac{x_1^2}{a^2} + \frac{x_2^2}{b^2} = 1$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive real numbers. The analysis focuses on the first eigenvalue associated with the first Robin eigenvalue problem. Additionally, the paper addresses the minimization of the anisotropic $p$-perimeter subject to a fixed area constraint.

Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNN) have become a vital tool for addressing problems involving data represented as graphs, such as those found in social networks or brain imaging. Within these networks, convolutional layers are responsible for integrating information from neighboring nodes, while pooling layers manage the reduction of graph structures. This paper presents a new methodology for implementing pooling operations on graphs, which can be applied to both weighted and unweighted data whether represented as adjacency matrices or signal vectors. The proposed technique is validated through experiments on graph classification tasks using well-established benchmark datasets.

Neural dependency parsing has become a popular approach for capturing rich contextual information in language, yet it demands substantial labeled datasets, which are costly and time-consuming to create. To address this limitation, we propose a novel semi-supervised graph-structured self-training method designed to enhance parsing performance. This technique leverages the predicted dependencies from an initial model to identify high-confidence unlabeled data, refining the model through multiple self-training iterations. Specifically, we introduce a re-weighted co-training mechanism that mitigates error propagation by focusing on reliable predictions across different views. Experiments conducted on standard English and Chinese datasets demonstrate that this approach significantly boosts performance compared to baseline methods.

This study examines the transition form factors governing the exclusive semileptonic decays $B\to D^{(*)}\ell\nu$ through a dispersion relation framework. By incorporating recent lattice QMC calculations for $B\to D$ and $B\to D^*$ in the $q^2\to 0$ limit, alongside lattice QMC results for $B\to D^{(*)}$ in the $q^2\to q^2_{\rm max}$ regime, we derive constraints on the remaining $q^2$ spectrum. Our analysis further demonstrates that the form factor $F_0(q^2)$ exhibits a pronounced sensitivity to the pole mass of the $b$-quark.

We present a duality-diode, a mechanism composed of dualities and symmetry operations that yields non-invertible symmetries in $\mathcal{N}=4$ supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories on $\mathbb{R}^{3,1}$. This approach applies specifically to both circular and rectangular non-supersymmetric theories derived via partial supersymmetry breaking.

The CFI-query involves determining if a specific non-isomorphic pair of vertices in a graph corresponds to a pair in another, where the relationship is preserved. This study examines the CFI-query through the lenses of both classical and counting first-order logic, alongside its extensions. It establishes that the query is CPT-definable precisely when the graph family has bounded clique-winning strategies, and similarly, it is $C_2L^{\infty}_{\infty}$-definable if the graphs exclude a topological minor. Additionally, the paper presents a counting logic query for graphs with bounded tree-depth, which can resolve the CFI-question for any such class.

Eu2Ir2O7 serves as a prototypical Weyl semimetal candidate, exhibiting a field-induced topological phase transition from a Chern insulator to a trivial insulator. This study examines the Eu2Ir2O7:Bi system, where Bi replaces Eu atoms, revealing a progressive suppression of the topological phase transition as doping increases. This suppression correlates with a reduction in the energy gap between the conduction and valence bands, a change driven by the narrowing of the conduction band. Furthermore, substituting Eu with elemental Bi triggers a novel phenomenon: a zero-field phase transition from a Chern insulator to a trivial one. These findings offer significant insights into the interplay between topology and magnetism, as well as the mechanisms behind the emergence of an effective magnetic field at the atomic scale.

This paper introduces a novel approach to examining the existence of Lipschitz selections for lower semicontinuous set-valued maps that have bounded variation and are defined on finite-dimensional spaces. Our primary existence theorem applies specifically to maps with a convex range, offering what we believe to be the optimal result within this specific framework. Additionally, we present several supporting findings that establish the case for maps with compact convex ranges under various supplementary conditions.

This study examines the statistical behavior of $n$-tuples $(X_1, \dots, X_n)$, where each $X_i$ is an independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) random variable drawn from a distribution with a density function. The analysis focuses on cyclic tuples, defined by the condition that the sum of their components equals zero.

We derive the asymptotic distribution for such cyclic tuples as $n$ increases. The limiting distribution is characterized by a specific density function, which is expressed as a convolution involving a uniform distribution on the hyperplane $\sum x_i = 0$ and a multivariate normal distribution.

Furthermore, we investigate the asymptotic properties of various functionals applied to these tuples. The results demonstrate that, as $n$ tends toward infinity, these properties converge to those observed in a standard Gaussian environment constrained to the aforementioned hyperplane.

This study examines the non-functional attributes of software systems resulting from run-time specialization configurations. It introduces a formal framework to define the property preservation problem, asking which preservation holds true when a system's run-time is configured. The findings demonstrate that altering a system's run-time configuration can either enhance or degrade its non-functional traits.
